latin.541: §. XI. De SECULO SEPTIMO quid nobis sperare liceat, quod ad confirmationem veritatis Eucharisticæ attinet, in aprico ponit Inscriptio à paulò ante allegato Mejero Helmstadiensi, eidem, hunc in modum, præfixa: In seculum septimum, communi doctorum Protestantium sententia, referuntur initia Anti-Christi, tam Orientalis quam Occidentalis: Unde insignes hôc seculo Status Religionis Christianæ passus est mutationes. Et quidem in Oriente non tam hæresis aliqua, aut secta, sed totius Religionis Christianæ occurrit excidium. In Occidente Pontifices Romani, Antichristiana dominatione statum Ecclesiæ Religionis Christianæ hactenus liberiorem, nunc servilem facere satagunt. §. 1. 52. p. 170. Cui præfixæ Inscriptioni accedat suffixa Paragraphi tertii: Veritatis testes, qui hoc seculo, mysterio iniquitatis contradixerunt, & Religionis Christianæ sinceritatem propagaverunt, numero oppido pauci fuerunt, quorum etiam aliquos ineptæ quæstiones occuparunt & exercuerunt, necessariâ doctrina neglectâ: Est enim Seculum VII. sterile scriptorum bonæ frugis. p. m. 171.
latin.542: Ut proinde nemini mirum videri debeat, si unum solum ISIDORUM, Episcopum Hispalensem, Veritatis hoc loco à nobis statuminandæ Possessorem advocemus, Lib. 1. de Offic. Eccles. c. 8. ita scribentem: Panis quia confirmat corpus nostrum, ideò corpus Christi nuncupatur, vinum autem quia sanguinem operatur in carne, ideo ad sanguinem Christi refertur. Hæc autem duo sunt visibilia; sanctificata tamen per Spiritum S. IN SACRAMENTUM DIVINI CORPORIS (non in substantiam corporis & sanguinis Christi) transeunt: Panis enim quem frangimus corpus Christi est, qui dicit, Ego sum Panis Vivus; Vinum autem, sanguis ejus est, & hoc est quod scriptum est, Ego sum vitis vera.
latin.543: Et adhuc clariùs Lib. 6. Etymolog. cap. 12. Sicuti enim substantia panis & vini visibilis, nutrit hominem exteriorem, ita verbum Christi, qui est panis vivus, PER PARTICIPATIONEM FIDEI, recreat animas fidelium. Quæ verba è Libris Isidori hodie impressis expuncta, à Bertramo Presbytero conservata nobis, Joh. Dunelmensis, Tract. crebrius cit. p. m. 84. observat.
latin.544: Isidoro Hispalensi sese proximè adjungit VENERABILIS BEDA, Britannicarum Insularum Doctor celeberrimus, quanquam octavo demum seculô Nomen ejus inclaruerit, non Eucharisticam duntaxat veritatem, Comment. in 22. Ps. palam hisce confessus: Loco carnis & sanguinis agni, substituit Christus Sacramentum carnis suæ & sanguinis, in FIGURA panis & vini. Item, Comm. in Psal. 3. Dedit in Cœna discipulis FIGURAM sacrosancti corporis & sanguinis sui;
latin.545: Sed & falsitatem, i. e. corporalem Christi, sive corporis ejus, tàm in terris hisce, quàm in Cœna S., præsentiam, seriò detestatus: Christus, inquit, ad patrem, post resurrectionem, Victor adscendens, Ecclesiam CORPORALITER reliquit, quam tamen nunquam divinæ præsidio præsentiæ destituit. Comment. in Marcum Lib. 4. cap. 13. Et in Joh. cap. 14. A quibus, ait, homo abscedebat Dominus, eos non relinquebat idem ipse Christus homo & Deus. Ergo ibat per id, quod homo erat, & manebat per id, quod Deus erat. Ibat per id, quod uno loco erat, & manebat per id, quod ubique erat.
latin.546: Denique in cap. Joh. sextum: Quisquis vivere vult, credat in Christum, manducet SPIRITUALITER SPIRITUALEM CIBUM incorporeum corporis Christi, & non sit putridum membrum.

pass_a.541: §. XI. What it is lawful for us to hope concerning the SEVENTH AGE, as to confirmation of the Eucharistic truth, the Inscription prefixed in this manner by Mejerus of Helmstedt, just now cited, sets in the open: To the seventh age, by the common sentence of Protestant doctors, are referred the beginnings of Anti-Christ, both Eastern and Western: Whence in this age the State of the Christian Religion suffered notable changes. And indeed in the East there occurred not so much some heresy or sect as the ruin of the whole Christian Religion. In the West the Roman Pontiffs, by Antichristian domination, strive to make the hitherto freer state of the Church of the Christian Religion now servile (§. 1. 52. p. 170). To which prefixed Inscription let there be added the suffix of the third Paragraph: The witnesses of Truth who in this age contradicted the mystery of iniquity and propagated the sincerity of the Christian Religion were exceedingly few in number, and even some of them inept questions occupied and exercised, necessary doctrine neglected: For the VIIth Age is sterile of writers of good fruit (p. m. 171).
pass_a.542: So that it ought to seem wonderful to no one if we summon as Possessor of the Truth to be propped up by us in this place one alone, ISIDORE, Bishop of Seville, writing thus in Book 1 On Ecclesiastical Offices ch. 8: Bread, because it confirms our body, is therefore called the body of Christ; but wine, because it works blood in the flesh, is therefore referred to the blood of Christ. But these two are visible; yet sanctified through the Holy Spirit they pass INTO THE SACRAMENT OF THE DIVINE BODY (not into the substance of the body and blood of Christ): For the bread which we break is the body of Christ, who says, I am the Living Bread; but the wine is His blood, and this is what is written, I am the true vine.
pass_a.543: And still more clearly Book 6 of the Etymologies ch. 12: For just as the visible substance of bread and wine nourishes the outer man, so the word of Christ, who is the living bread, THROUGH THE PARTICIPATION OF FAITH, recreates the souls of the faithful. Which words, struck out from the books of Isidore printed today, but preserved for us by Bertram the Presbyter, John of Durham observes in the Tract more often cited (p. m. 84).
pass_a.544: To Isidore of Seville there joins himself most nearly the VENERABLE BEDE, most celebrated Doctor of the British Isles, although his Name first became famous only in the eighth age — having confessed not only the Eucharistic truth openly in these words in the Commentary on Psalm 22: In place of the flesh and blood of the lamb, Christ substituted the Sacrament of His flesh and blood, in the FIGURE of bread and wine. Likewise, Commentary on Psalm 3: He gave at the Supper to the disciples the FIGURE of His sacrosanct body and blood;
pass_a.545: But he also seriously detested the falsehood, i.e. the corporal presence of Christ, or of His body, both on these earths and in the Sacred Supper: Christ, he says, ascending Victor to the Father after the resurrection, left the Church CORPORALLY, which yet He never stripped of the guard of divine presence (Commentary on Mark Book 4 ch. 13). And on John ch. 14: Those from whom the Lord was departing as man, the same Christ Himself man and God was not leaving. Therefore He was going by that which He was as man, and remaining by that which He was as God. He was going by that which was in one place, and remaining by that which was everywhere.
pass_a.546: Finally on the sixth chapter of John: Whoever wishes to live, let him believe in Christ, let him eat SPIRITUALLY the SPIRITUAL FOOD, the incorporeal of Christ’s body, and not be a putrid member.

541: §.XI: what hope for the SEVENTH age confirming Eucharistic truth? Mejerus puts it in the open.

Protestant doctors refer Anti-Christ’s beginnings (East and West) to this age — East: ruin of whole religion; West: Rome drives the Church toward servitude. Truth-witnesses few; Age VII sterile of good writers.
542: So Strimesius summons one alone: ISIDORE of Seville (de Offic. Eccles. 1.8).

Bread is called Christ’s body because it confirms ours; wine referred to His blood because it works blood in the flesh — visible things that, sanctified, pass INTO THE SACRAMENT OF THE DIVINE BODY (not into the substance of body and blood).
543: Clearer still (Etymolog. 6.12): visible bread and wine nourish the outer man; Christ’s word, the living bread, recreates faithful souls THROUGH THE PARTICIPATION OF FAITH.
Those words are struck from today’s printed Isidore — preserved by Bertram the Presbyter (John of Durham notes).
544: Next to Isidore: the VENERABLE BEDE (British Isles’ doctor; name famous mainly in the eighth age).

On Ps. 22: in place of the lamb’s flesh and blood Christ put the Sacrament of His flesh and blood in the FIGURE of bread and wine. On Ps. 3: at the Supper He gave the disciples the FIGURE of His sacrosanct body and blood.
545: Bede also seriously detests the falsehood of a corporal presence of Christ or His body — on earth or in the Sacred Supper.

Ascending Victor after the resurrection He left the Church CORPORALLY, yet never without divine presence. As man He went; as God He remained — going as in one place, remaining as everywhere (Mark 4.13; John 14).
546: On John 6: whoever would live, believe in Christ and eat SPIRITUALLY the SPIRITUAL FOOD — the incorporeal of Christ’s body — and not be a putrid member.
